correctness.rationale: In odd characteristic, diagonalize S. Invertible T sends each S-eigenspace isomorphically onto the other, and T²=I gives the normal form with S=diag(I,−I) and T the block swap. In an isometry group the eigenspaces are orthogonal and nondegenerate, with isometric restrictions. Hence simultaneous isometry orbits are classified by W with V isometric to W⊥W, and the pair stabilizer is exactly the diagonal copy of Isom(W) (or GL(W) with no form). The finite-field form classifications give one Hermitian type, one alternating type only in even half-dimension, and two m-dimensional symmetric types. Both symmetric doubles have square Gram determinant, exactly the necessary ambient class; the even-dimensional Witt sign is the character of (−1)^m det B. Both generators have determinant (−1)^m. For m even the special-orbit quotient is the ambient determinant image modulo the stabilizer determinant image: squares in the multiplicative and norm-one groups, trivial in the orthogonal case. The ambient determinant maps are onto (use a single diagonal norm-one entry in a unitary orthonormal basis or a reflection for O), giving the asserted equal splits. Since (ST)²=−I, the generators are reflections of an embedded D8; for each of its four reflections only the two with odd difference of reflection exponents give (ST)²=−I. This gives eight ordered generators per subgroup and does not count subgroup conjugacy classes. Independent enumeration of orthonormal frames and literal matrix conjugation over F3 verified the O4+ orbit sizes 144,288 and SO4+ sizes 72,72,144,144, including the four-way special splitting.
residual_risks: The finite reproduction tests an orthogonal boundary case, not all q or all types. The proof requires odd characteristic and actual involutive lifts; projective, spinor-norm and subgroup conjugacy class questions are excluded.

evidence: Taylor–Vinroot enumerate single involutions by eigenspace types. De Franceschi describes centralizers of single semisimple elements. Resultary 5a4123fce03b counts unrestricted anticommuting tuples of 2×2 matrices, not marked pairs of isometric involutions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The single-involution stabilizer generally allows independent changes on the two eigenspaces. Enforcing T reduces it to the diagonal group and changes its determinant image. These single-element results do not themselves provide the joint special-subgroup orbit counts.

evidence: The dual-number record obtains AB=−BA for distinct commuting projective residue involutions, and in the frozen problem ST=−TS does imply projective commutation.
Standard single-involution counts can be used to compute a pair total once its isometric eigenspace and permitted intertwiner constraints are derived.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Projective commutation does not require anticommuting lifts squaring to I; one cannot turn projective Klein-four totals into these marked D8 counts wholesale. Single-element results supply inputs but neither impose the exchange isometry between eigenspaces nor determine the special orbit splitting of the joint stabilizer.

evidence: Putting r=ST and s=S gives representations of the marked D8 with r² sent to −I; conversely T=sr. The related Jones–Keller paper studies orbits of a D8 action on a vector space, not conjugacy or totals of such representations into target groups.
Chen–Wang classify components of the complex anticommuting matrix variety without involution or form constraints.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Counting marked D8 representations with prescribed central action is genuinely equivalent. General representation recoding and the usual orbit method are standard, but the inspected work does not give counts or determinant-one refinements for that equivalent problem. Component classification of a larger variety is not the orbit classification of this constrained finite set.

originality.rationale: Credit the classical eigenspace methods, form classification and centralizer framework; the surviving supported contribution is the uniform ordered-pair and embedded-subgroup census with the determinant-one and orthogonal-type refinements. Inspected related results cover individual involutions, an unrestricted pair variety, or a different lift problem. This verdict is a bounded comparison, not a claim that the underlying representation theory or every low-dimensional case is new.
residual_risks: Further equivalent enumeration in finite classical subgroup or representation literature may exist. The normal form is elementary, and novelty is scoped to the exact combined census and splitting results.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md, census and determinant-image argument
value.rationale: This answers a natural embedding-count question with marked central element rather than a single ad hoc instance. The form on a half-space distinguishes orthogonal orbits even when the stabilizer orders agree, and the determinant quotient reveals genuinely different simultaneous orbits despite unchanged pair totals. This makes the census usable for comparing full and special groups and extracting actual embedded subgroup numbers.
residual_risks: No classification of conjugacy classes of embedded D8 subgroups or statistics of all projective involutions.
